document.lead: You should spend about 40 minutes on this task.
after: Give reasons for your answer and include any relevant examples from your own knowledge or experience.

text: It is true that in many parts of the world, people are eating poorly, taking little exercise and spending long hours sitting down. This trend creates serious problems for both individuals and society, but there are practical steps that could reduce them.

The most obvious problem is the rise in illnesses such as diabetes, heart disease and obesity. These conditions not only reduce the quality of life of those who suffer from them but also place a heavy burden on health services, which have to spend large sums of money on long-term treatment. In addition, unhealthy people are more likely to take time off work, so businesses lose productivity and the economy suffers as a result. Mental health can also suffer, because people who do little exercise often feel more stressed and tired, and this reduces their ability to enjoy daily life.

To tackle this issue, governments should start by promoting healthy habits from an early age. Schools could provide nutritious meals and make physical education compulsory, so that children learn to value exercise. Moreover, a tax on sugary drinks and fast food, like the one introduced in the UK, would discourage people from buying the least healthy products, and the revenue could be used to build parks and sports facilities. Employers can also help by offering gym memberships or flexible hours for exercise. Finally, local authorities can organise free exercise classes in parks, which would make it easier for people on low incomes to stay active.

In conclusion, unhealthy lifestyles lead to serious medical and economic problems, but a combination of education, taxation and workplace support could encourage people to make better choices and gradually reverse the trend.

document.title: Unhealthy lifestyles
document.question:
In many countries, more and more people are leading unhealthy lifestyles.

What problems does this cause, and what can be done to solve them?
